title: Composition of Koszul-regular scheme immersions
statement: Let $Z,Y,X$ be schemes [def-pc-scheme], and let $i:Z\to Y$ and $j:Y\to X$ be immersions [def-weil-closed-immersion]. Call an immersion $a:A\to B$ Koszul-regular if locally at every point of $A$ it is a closed immersion into an open subscheme of $B$ and its ideal there is locally generated by a finite Koszul-regular sequence [def-weil-pbc-koszul-regular-sequence]. The empty sequence is allowed. If $i$ and $j$ are Koszul-regular, then $j\circ i$ is Koszul-regular. No Noetherian, flatness, separation, or fixed-codimension hypothesis is imposed.

proof.text: The composite $c=j\circ i$ is an immersion by clause (e) of [lem-weil-pbc-proper-fp-permanence], applied to the two given immersions. It remains to check the local Koszul-regular ideal condition at each $z\in Z$.

Fix $z\in Z$, $y=i(z)$ and $x=j(y)$. Factor $j$ as a closed immersion into an open $W\subseteq X$, and factor $i$ as a closed immersion into an open $V\subseteq Y$ [def-weil-closed-immersion]. Since $Y$ is closed in $W$, the closed subset $Y\setminus V$ is closed in $W$. Replacing $W$ by $W\setminus(Y\setminus V)$ replaces $Y$ by $V$; thus both arrows are closed immersions on these neighbourhoods. The Koszul-regular ideal conditions restrict to these opens. At every point of $V$ the local Koszul-regular condition of the statement for $j$ is the local condition of [lem-sfb-koszul-closed-immersion-affine-criterion]: generating sections over a neighbourhood whose germs form a Koszul-regular sequence at every point of it, i.e. the sheaf Koszul complex is acyclic in positive degrees (Stacks 063D); where the given neighbourhood is affine with generators Koszul-regular in its ring, the reverse direction of that criterion supplies this. The same holds for $i$ at the points of $Z$ over $V$. Apply [lem-sfb-koszul-closed-immersion-affine-criterion] to $j$ and choose $U=\operatorname{Spec}A$ containing $x$ such that $Y_U=\operatorname{Spec}B$, $B=A/I$, with $I=(f_1,\ldots,f_n)$ and $f$ Koszul-regular in $A$. Here and below source restrictions mean full inverse images of the indicated opens, so the point $z$ is retained. The affine descriptions and ideal sheaves are those of [def-weil-closed-immersion] and [def-sbc-closed-immersion-ideal-sheaf].

The restricted $i$ is a Koszul-regular closed immersion into $\operatorname{Spec}B$. The principal-neighbourhood clause of [lem-sfb-koszul-closed-immersion-affine-criterion] supplies $\bar h\in B$ not vanishing at $y$, such that over $D(\bar h)$ its ideal is generated by a Koszul-regular tuple $\bar g_1,\ldots,\bar g_m\in B_{\bar h}$. Lift $\bar h$ to $h\in A$. Then $B_{\bar h}=A_h/IA_h$ by [lem-weil-pbc-localization-quotient-commute]. The images of $f$ generate $IA_h$ and remain Koszul-regular: $A\to A_h$ is flat by [lem-weil-pbc-localization-flat], and [lem-sc-koszul-regular-flat-base-change] applies. Replace $A$ by $A_h$, $B$ by $B_{\bar h}$ and $I$ by $IA_h$; lift each $\bar g_k$ to $g_k\in A$. All points under consideration survive because $\bar h(y)\ne0$.

On these affine opens the composite is induced by the surjection $A\to B/(\bar g_1,\ldots,\bar g_m)$. Its kernel is $J=(f_1,\ldots,f_n,g_1,\ldots,g_m)$: an element mapping to zero is a linear combination of the $g_k$ modulo $I$, and lifting its coefficients leaves an element of $I=(f)$. Conversely every $f_i$ and $g_k$ maps to zero. The affine closed-immersion description identifies its defining ideal with this kernel [def-weil-closed-immersion, def-sbc-closed-immersion-ideal-sheaf].

The quotient augmentations $K_A(f)\to B[0]$ and $K_B(\bar g)\to(B/(\bar g))[0]$ are quasi-isomorphisms. Indeed, in the explicit Koszul complex [def-weil-pbc-koszul-complex] one has $K_0=A$ and $d_1(e_i)=f_i$, so its zeroth homology is $A/(f)$ and the augmentation is that quotient identification. All positive homology vanishes by Koszul regularity [def-weil-pbc-koszul-regular-sequence], and negative chain degrees vanish. The identical calculation over $B$ gives the second augmentation. Reindex to the cohomological degrees $[-n,0]$ and $[-m,0]$ used in the next step.

Apply the concatenation clause of [lem-sfb-koszul-evaluation-pasting] with $S=A$, its tuple $f$, quotient $B=A/(f)$, second tuple $g$, and $D=B/(\bar g)$. Its hypotheses are precisely the two quotient-augmentation quasi-isomorphisms just checked. The clause says that the augmented Koszul complex on the ordered concatenation $(f,g)$ resolves $D$. Hence its positive chain homology vanishes, so $(f,g)$ is Koszul-regular by [def-weil-pbc-koszul-regular-sequence]. This uses only the resolution clause, not the evaluation or sign compatibilities of that node.

proof.text: Thus the defining ideal $J$ of the composite on the constructed affine neighbourhood of $x$ is generated by a finite Koszul-regular sequence. Its affine-chart hypothesis holds for the closed immersion $c^{-1}(\operatorname{Spec}A)\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ at every point $t$ of the source: for an open $O\ni c(t)$ choose $k\in A$ with $c(t)\in D(k)\subseteq O$; then $A_k$ is flat over $A$ [lem-weil-pbc-localization-flat], the images of $(f,g)$ are Koszul-regular in $A_k$ [lem-sc-koszul-regular-flat-base-change], and they generate the ideal $JA_k$ of $c^{-1}(D(k))=\operatorname{Spec}(A_k/JA_k)$ [lem-weil-pbc-localization-quotient-commute]. The reverse implication of [lem-sfb-koszul-closed-immersion-affine-criterion] therefore gives the local ideal condition for $c$ near $z$; directly, $D(h)$ with the tuple $(f,g)$ in its ring is also such a neighbourhood. As $z$ was arbitrary and $c$ is already an immersion, this is exactly the Koszul-regularity required in the statement. If $Z$ is empty there are no points to check. Neither empty tuple was excluded; its Koszul complex is the ring in degree zero, so the same argument includes either arrow having zero defining ideal.
